title: Equation of tangents and normal lines to curves
competency: Write the equations of tangent and normal lines and find vertical tangents.

keywords.def: The line perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency.
A line that touches a curve at one point and has its steepness there.

en.text: The tangent at x = a has slope f′(a): y = f′(a)(x − a) + f(a). The normal is perpendicular, slope −1/f′(a). If f′(a) = 0 the tangent is horizontal and the normal is the vertical line x = a. A vertical tangent can occur where f′ is undefined because its denominator becomes 0.

am.text: በ x = a ላይ ያለው ታንጀንት ስሎፕ f′(a) አለው፤ y = f′(a)(x − a) + f(a)። ኖርማሉ ቀጥ ያለ ነው፣ ስሎፑ −1/f′(a)።

screens.title: A line that touches
screens.ask: A curve has slope 3 at (−2, 5). Which line is the tangent there?
screens.after:
Point-slope form: y − 5 = 3(x − (−2)) = 3(x + 2).
y = 3x + 6 + 5 = 3x + 11.
Check: at x = −2, y = −6 + 11 = 5. ✓
y = 3x + 5 has the right slope but misses the point.

screens.title: Tangent and normal lines
paras: Tangent at (a, f(a)): y = f′(a)(x − a) + f(a).
The normal line is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency.
screens.note: If f′(a) = 0: tangent y = f(a), normal x = a.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The line perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency.
A line that touches a curve at one point and has its steepness there.

screens.text: Find the tangent line to f(x) = x³ − 2x at (1, −1):
screens.why:
f′(x) = 3x² − 2, so f′(1) = 3 − 2 = 1.
Tangent: y = f′(1)(x − 1) + f(1) = 1(x − 1) − 1.
y = x − 2.
Check: at x = 1, y = −1. ✓
Trap: y = 3x − 4 uses 3x² = 3 and forgets the −2.

screens.title: Tangent and normal to y = x²
screens.note: Tangent: y = 2a(x − a) + a². Tangent slope × normal slope is always −1.

screens.text: Find the normal line to f(x) = x³ + x + 2 at (0, 2):
screens.why:
f′(x) = 3x² + 1, so f′(0) = 1.
Normal slope = −1/f′(0) = −1.
Normal: y = −1(x − 0) + 2 = −x + 2.
Trap: y = x + 2 is the tangent, not the normal.

screens.ask: Use the product rule to find the tangent slope of f(x) = (1 − x³)√(x + 2) at (−1, 2): ___

screens.text: Find where f(x) = √(x² − x) has vertical tangents (tap all):
screens.why:
f′(x) = (2x − 1)/(2√(x² − x)).
The bottom is 0 when x² − x = x(x − 1) = 0: x = 0 or x = 1.
There the top is −1 or 1, not 0, so the slope blows up.
Points: (0, 0) and (1, 0).
x = 1/2 is not in the domain (x² − x < 0 there).
screens.clue: Where is the denominator of f′ zero?

screens.text: True or false: if the tangent slope is 4, the normal slope is −4.
screens.why:
Perpendicular slopes multiply to −1.
Normal slope = −1/4.
Check: 4 × (−1/4) = −1. ✓
−4 only flips the sign; it is not perpendicular. False.

screens.ask: Find the unknown: f(x) = x² + ax + b and g(x) = x³ − c share the same tangent at (1, 2). a = ___
screens.why:
Same tangent means same slope at x = 1.
g′(x) = 3x², so g′(1) = 3.
f′(x) = 2x + a, so f′(1) = 2 + a.
2 + a = 3 gives a = 1.
(Then f(1) = 2 gives b = 0, and g(1) = 2 gives c = −1.)

items.text: Find the tangent line to f(x) = x³ + x + 2 at (0, 2):
Find the normal line to f(x) = (1 − x³)√(x + 2) at (−1, 2):
items.why:
Tangent slope f′(−1) = −2 (product rule).
Normal slope = −1/(−2) = 1/2.
y = (1/2)(x + 1) + 2 = x/2 + 5/2.
Trap: y = −2x is a line with the tangent's slope.

items.text: Find where f(x) = √(x² − x) has vertical tangents (tap all):
items.why:
f′ = (2x − 1)/(2√(x² − x)).
The bottom is 0 when x² − x = 0: x = 0 or 1.
Points (0, 0) and (1, 0).

items.text: Find where f(x) = 2√x has a vertical tangent:
items.why:
f′(x) = 1/√x.
At x = 0 the bottom is 0: f′ is undefined and the slope blows up.
f(0) = 0, so the point is (0, 0).

items.text: x² + ax + b and x³ − c share the tangent at (1, 2). Find the common normal line:
items.why:
Common tangent slope: g′(1) = 3.
Normal slope = −1/3.
y = −(1/3)(x − 1) + 2 = −x/3 + 1/3 + 2.
y = −x/3 + 7/3.

test.ask: Find the slope of the normal to f(x) = x² at (2, 4): ___
test.why:
Tangent slope f′(2) = 2 × 2 = 4.
Normal slope = −1/4 (negative reciprocal).
Check: 4 × (−1/4) = −1. ✓

test.text: Find the normal line to f(x) = x² − 4x at x = 2:
test.why:
f′(x) = 2x − 4, so f′(2) = 0.
The tangent is horizontal: y = f(2) = −4.
A line perpendicular to a horizontal line is vertical.
Normal: x = 2.
Trap: y = −4 is the tangent.

test.ask: Find where the tangent to f(x) = √x at x = 4 meets the y-axis: y = ___
Find where the tangent to f(x) = 1/x at (1, 1) meets the x-axis: x = ___
test.why:
f′(x) = −1/x², so f′(1) = −1.
Tangent: y = −(x − 1) + 1 = 2 − x.
At the x-axis y = 0: x = 2.

screens.text: Find the slope of the tangent to f(x) = x³ at x = −1:
screens.why:
f′(x) = 3x².
f′(−1) = 3(−1)² = 3 × 1 = 3.
Trap: −3 forgets that (−1)² is positive.
screens.clue: Square of a negative is positive.
